name: Lechweg
kurzbeschreibung: The alpine opening section of the Lechweg on the Arlberg leads from Lake Formarinsee at 1,793 m beneath the Rote Wand through pristine gorges and Walser hamlets to Steeg.
preis: Trail free of charge; Formarinsee shuttle bus approx. €15.00 (free with Lech Card)
oeffnungszeiten: Mid-June to early October (subject to snow conditions)
beschreibung:
Overview

The alpine section Lechweg Arlberg marks the dramatic opening of Europe's first long-distance hiking trail certified as a "Leading Quality Trail – Best of Europe". Starting at 1,793 metres above sea level near emerald-green Lake Formarinsee beneath the towering limestone walls of the Rote Wand, the Lech River begins its wild journey. Where the Formarinbach and Spullerbach streams merge, one of the last genuine wild rivers of the Northern Limestone Alps springs to life. This high-alpine itinerary leads hikers from the pristine headwaters through traditional Walser mountain settlements like Lech am Arlberg and Warth, crossing into Tyrol towards Steeg. Rushing alpine torrents, Swiss stone pine forests, lush flower meadows, and jagged mountain ridges create an unforgettable wilderness experience far removed from mass tourism.

Route & Requirements

The initial three day-stages span approximately 40 kilometres along alpine singletracks, root-covered paths, and gravel riverbanks. Hikers need sure-footedness, a head for heights along exposed cliffside trails, and good baseline physical fitness for daily walking times of four to six hours. Ankle-high hiking boots with grippy lug soles, functional mountain clothing, and trekking poles are indispensable. Specific narrow rock passages within the young Lech river gorge are secured with steel safety cables. Due to the high-alpine terrain, the trail is unsuitable for pushchairs or wheelchairs. Dogs are welcome on the trail but must strictly be kept on a lead across working alpine pastures and grazing meadows.

Visit & Arrival

The optimal hiking season runs from mid-June to early October once high-altitude mountain passes are clear of snow. The tour departs from Alpe Formarin at Lake Formarinsee, accessible by regular hikers' shuttle bus from Lech am Arlberg during summer. Motorists reach Lech via the Inntal A12 or Rheintal A14 motorways and the Arlberg expressway S16 over the Flexenpass road (B198). Rail travellers take express trains to Langen am Arlberg, connecting directly with VVT and Landbus line 750 to Lech Zürs.

Tips

Catch the first morning hikers' bus up to Lake Formarinsee: on calm mornings, the mighty Rote Wand is mirrored flawlessly in the crystal-clear water, creating one of the most photographed vistas in the Alps. Acquire the regional Lech Card to enjoy free rides on local summer lifts and hiker buses.
